language.sample_text: この先工事中 — 注意
language.script_notes: Standard Japanese as national. Place names sometimes derive from Ainu language roots (e.g. many end in -betsu, -nai).

road_furniture.bollard_color: White as national, but noticeably taller in heavy-snow areas so they remain visible above snowbanks.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Slim posts, elevated/taller variants near passes and rural roads.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: White guardrail with red-and-white chevron reflector stickers; occasional orange stickers.
road_furniture.line_paint: White/yellow center lines as national, though often snow-covered or faded in winter imagery.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal or absent on rural roads; wide paved shoulders instead.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Red-and-white striped snow poles (down-pointing arrows) mark the road edge above the snow line — a strong Hokkaido-specific tell. Roads are noticeably wider than the rest of Japan to leave room for snow removal and piled snowbanks.

architecture.roof_style: Steep-pitched roofs designed for heavy snow load; many houses raised or built with above-ground utility connections to survive snow depth.
architecture.roof_material: Metal roofing, often brightly coloured (blue, green, red) rather than the grey ceramic tile typical further south.
architecture.wall_construction: Detached houses with more space between them than crowded mainland cities; larger farm structures reflecting Hokkaido's agricultural land.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bright primary-colour metal roofs against muted wall siding; utility poles less densely packed than in Honshu cities.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Large dairy/agricultural barns, wide low-density farmhouses, ski-resort infrastructure, Sapporo's grid-planned city blocks.

nature.vegetation: Broad-leafed 'cabbage-looking' alpine shrubs and grassland at altitude; birch and coniferous forest; large flat agricultural plains (Tokachi, Furano) unlike mountainous mainland Japan.
nature.terrain: More open and flatter in the agricultural plains than the rest of Japan, with volcanic mountains (Daisetsuzan) and caldera lakes; less densely forested-and-squeezed than Honshu.
nature.climate_signature: Cold, snowy winters with long-lasting snow cover; imagery frequently shows snowbanks, bare trees and grey skies — much colder-looking than the rest of Japan.

vehicles.plate_format: Two-line kanji + hiragana + digits format as national; top line reads a Hokkaido regional office name (e.g. 札幌, 函館).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: More 4WD and Subarus than the national average given snow and rural terrain; snowplow and agricultural equipment common in season.

google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Japan low-mounted-camera blur as national.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage along main routes and towns; larger gaps in remote mountain/agricultural areas than central Honshu. Snowy imagery common outside summer.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script, same plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Hokkaido's noticeably wider roads, red-and-white snow poles, and flatter agricultural plains (Tokachi/Furano) distinguish it from Honshu's narrower, more mountainous, densely built roads.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cold snowy climate, wide roads, similar-looking rural infrastructure
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Japan drives on the LEFT with Japanese script and yellow-black striped poles; the Russian Far East drives on the right with Cyrillic and Soviet panel-block architecture.
